lines: Title: Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 2
Let $\mathbf C, \mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be [[Definition:Category|categories]].

Let $F, G : \mathbf C \times \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be [[Definition:Bifunctor|bifunctors]] from the [[Definition:Product Category|product category]] $\mathbf C \times \mathbf D$ to the [[Definition:Category|category]] $\mathbf E$.
denote the [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the first variable]] of $F$ and $G$, respectively, with $C$.
denote the [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the second variable]] of $F$ and $G$, respectively, with $D$.
For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $\tuple{C, D} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D$ let:
:$\alpha : F \to G$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]

:$(1)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C : \alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]

:$(2)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D : \alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
:for [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|objects]] $C \in \mathbf C$ and $D \in \mathbf D$, $\alpha \tuple{-, D}_C = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D}}$
=== [[Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 2 Necessary Condition|Necessary Condition]] ===
Let $\alpha : F \to G$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]].

:for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', g:D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D : \map G {f, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D'} } \circ \map F {f, g}$

:$(3)\quad$ for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', \operatorname{id}_D:D \to D} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D : \map G {f, \operatorname{id}_D} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C', D} } \circ \map F {f, \operatorname{id}_D}$

:$(4)\quad$ for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{\operatorname{id}_C: C \to C, g:D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D : \map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g}$
For all [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $D \in \mathbf D$ and [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$, we have:
It follows that for each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D$:
:$\alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
For all [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]] $C \in \mathbf C$ and [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $g: D \to D' \in \mathbf D$, we have:
It follows that for each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C$:
:$\alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
=== [[Characterization of Natural Transformation Between Bifunctors/Proof 2 Sufficient Condition|Sufficient Condition]] ===

:$(1)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $C \in \mathbf C : \alpha \tuple{C, -} : F \tuple{C, -} \to G \tuple{C, -}$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]

:$(2)\quad$ For each [[Definition:Object (Category Theory)|object]]  $D \in \mathbf D : \alpha \tuple{-, D} : F \tuple{-, D} \to G \tuple{-, D}$ be a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]]
:for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g:D \to D' \in \mathbf D$:
::$\map {G \tuple{-, D} } f \circ \alpha \tuple{-, D}_C = \alpha \tuple{-, D}_{C'} \circ \map {F \tuple{-, D} } f$
:for all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $f: C \to C' \in \mathbf C$ and $g:D \to D' \in \mathbf D$:
::$(4)\quad \map G {\operatorname{id}_C, g} \circ \alpha_{\tuple{C, D} } = \alpha_{\tuple{C, D'} } \circ \map F {\operatorname{id}_C, g}$
:* [[Definition:Functor|functors]] obtained by [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the first variable]] and [[Definition:Bifunctor|substituting the second variable]]
For all [[Definition:Morphism (Category Theory)|morphisms]] $\tuple{f: C \to C', g:D \to D'} \in \mathbf C \times \mathbf D$, we have:
It follows that $\alpha: F \to G$ is a [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformation]] by definition.{{qed}}
